---
name: saga-trace-filename-claims
description: saga's Stop hook extracts claims from filenames named in the final message, so only name files actually changed or run
metadata:
  type: project
---

The `saga hook claude-code Stop` trace layer scrapes the final assistant message for
claims and checks them against the real diff and command log. Naming a file path in
prose is read as "touched <path>" and is contradicted as `not_in_diff` if that file is
unchanged; an execution verb near a filename ("running it would have deleted x.js") is
read as "ran x.js" and contradicted as `not_executed`. This blocks the stop even when
the underlying work is correct.

**Why:** explaining which files I deliberately left alone is normally good reporting, but
here every mention of an untouched path registers as a false claim and blocks completion.

**How to apply:** in the final message, name only files actually modified or commands
actually executed. Describe files left intact generically ("the hand-maintained files
under build/") and cite the contract gate that asserts they are unchanged instead of
listing paths. Diagnose blocks with `saga trace claims <run-id>`, which labels each
extracted claim verified/unverified/contradicted.
- [saga trace filename claims](saga-trace-filename-claims.md) — the Stop hook turns filenames in your summary into claims it will contradict
